newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cockerill shares slide on 1997 outlook.
newsitem.headline: Cockerill shares slide on 1997 outlook.

text.p: Shares in Belgian steel maker Cockerill Sambre shed 11 francs or 8.3 percent to 122 by midsession on Wednesday after visiting analysts heard the company give a discouraging outlook for 1997.

"The company reiterated that 1996 was bad in terms of results...(while) 1997 would not be a good year - and probably a gloomy year if steel prices stay at these levels," steel analyst Olivier Heuschling said.
"So far they are not expecting a rise in steel prices," he added. Analysts also noted Cockerill had risen sharply from 115 francs on January 2, a move they considered exaggerated.
"Even though we think the share is still undervalued, for a sustained move you need good news as well -- the trigger would be a steel price increase," Heuschling added.

Another analyst noted flat steel makers such as Cockerill and Sidmar, a Belgian unit of Luxembourg-based group Arbed, had recently renewed their annual contracts to supply car makers at less favourable prices than before.
